newsitem.title: USA: Swearing can be good for you, says U.S. researcher.
newsitem.headline: Swearing can be good for you, says U.S. researcher.

text.p: Swearing is sometimes good for you and may reduce stress, a University of Florida researcher said on Tuesday.

"We have been told all our lives that swearing is inappropriate, but there are actually times when it may be appropriate," said Kristy Beers, a doctoral candidate in linguistics, adding that it can relieve stress.
Beers said swear words have become more acceptable in daily speech and noted that words that were taboo a decade or two ago are now heard on prime time television.
People tend to take on other people's way of speaking when they are together, including swear words, she said. These words can also be used as a way to identify with a group of people.
"In the back of everyone's mind we have rules, but what is more important than the rules is the company we are in. The company we are in overrides the environment and the rules," Beers said.
